clue.text: It's below the belt and sounds a bit fishy!

definitions.text: It's below the belt and sounds a bit fishy!

parts.note: surface reading: an unfair blow or a dodgy remark
setter's reading: the garment's name says it is a portion of a common white fish

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark about something suspicious going on below the waistline.
explanation.walkthrough: Fishy suggests suspicious, but it is literal: the name is a portion of the fish used in fish and chips.
explanation.definitionFit: A codpiece was a pouch worn at the front of men's breeches, sitting just under the waist.

clue.text: Copper raised vehicle certificates and tax

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the word is written upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: MOTs are the annual roadworthiness certificates for British vehicles

explanation.surface: A list of paperwork and levies attached to running a car.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is the yearly safety test a British car must pass; its plural turned upwards follows CU.
explanation.definitionFit: Customs duties are a tax on imports, and custom alone is an old word for such a levy.

clue.text: Mended by sailors coming in late, upset

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so one piece goes inside the other
upset in a down entry means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: the late person is one who has died
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Something was repaired by sailors who arrived late and in a bad mood.
explanation.walkthrough: DEAD turned up becomes DAED, and the navy goes into its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To darn is to mend a hole in fabric by weaving thread across it, as with socks.

clue.text: In study prepared true contract

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something prepared has been worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a den is a private study room
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A genuine agreement was drawn up while sitting in the study.
explanation.definitionFit: An indenture is a formal legal agreement, especially one binding an apprentice to a master.

clue.text: Traditional nunnery by holy island lake

parts.note: a convent is a house of nuns
Iona is the Scottish island where St Columba founded his monastery
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A description of an old-fashioned convent standing beside a lake on a sacred island.
explanation.walkthrough: Iona, off western Scotland, is the stock crossword holy island.
explanation.definitionFit: Conventional and traditional both describe following long-established customs and accepted ways of doing things.

clue.text: Spirits provided by good landlords

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a landlord of a pub is the host

explanation.surface: Drinks served by friendly pub landlords.
explanation.walkthrough: Spirits looks like drink to go with the landlords, but it means phantoms.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghosts are the departed souls of the dead, which are also called spirits.

clue.text: Women's quarters and hospital are by motorway

parts.note: H is the map symbol for hospital
taken as written
M is the British prefix for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: Female lodgings and a hospital sit beside a major road.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the separate part of a Muslim household where the women live.

clue.text: Isolate a tree sap comes from

indicators.note: the answer is said to come out of these letters, made from them in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Sap oozes from a tree, and we are told to set that tree apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate something is to set it apart from others, which is what isolating does.

clue.text: Skulking by lift, they drop key

parts.note: to lift is to steal

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it go, so a letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: Burglars creeping about drop a key while using a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: Lift means pinch, not elevator; THEY loses its E to leave THY.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy describes moving quietly and secretly to avoid notice, which is what skulking means.

clue.text: Clashing with walk by conservationists

parts.note: a stride is a long step in walking
the NT, National Trust, is a British heritage conservation charity; by places it after

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out on a walk organised by conservation campaigners.
explanation.definitionFit: Strident means loud and harsh, as clashing sounds are when they jar on the ear.

clue.text: Journey the Parisian made three times

parts.note: a trip is a journey
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A Parisian took the same journey three times over.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is read as a verb: to triple is to make something three times as great.
explanation.definitionFit: To triple a quantity is to multiply it by three, making it threefold.

clue.text: Defects turning up in trousers

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: shorts are short trousers
to turn up is to arrive or come

explanation.surface: Flaws in a pair of trousers, such as cuffs turning up.
explanation.walkthrough: Turning up suggests trouser turn-ups or a reversal, but it simply means arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortcomings are failings or faults, the ways something falls below standard.

clue.text: Once a stormy sea

indicators.note: a stormy state is turbulent, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A sea that was once rough.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean is a vast body of salt water, a sea in the broad sense.

clue.text: Quiet meal here turned out to be short-lived

indicators.note: turned out suggests contents tipped out and rearranged

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical marking for quiet
taken as written, to be mixed with the P

explanation.surface: A peaceful dinner here ended up being brief.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemeral things last only a very short time, from Greek for lasting a day.

clue.text: Sweet goat from Scotland?

parts.note: a goat is something that butts, a butter
Scotch means Scottish

explanation.surface: Asking whether a nice goat comes from Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: A butter here is one who butts, as goats do. Butterscotch is a hard toffee made with butter and brown sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterscotch is a confection, and in British English a sweet is a piece of confectionery.

clue.text: Kind of sale which snooker players hope to make?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sale clearing old stock at reduced prices

definitions.text: which snooker players hope to make
definitions.meaning: second meaning: potting all the remaining balls in one visit to the table

explanation.walkthrough: Snooker is a cue sport played on a large table; potting every remaining ball in one turn is a total clearance.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a shop sale emptying stock and, in snooker, potting all balls left on the table.

clue.text: Sure cad's rebuilt these second-hand vehicles

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again in a different form

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A shady dealer is confident about the bodged-up old motors he sells.
explanation.definitionFit: Used cars are vehicles that have had previous owners, the trade's term for second-hand vehicles.

clue.text: Spoiling mother, getting old

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
growing old is aging

explanation.surface: Pampering an elderly mother as she gets older.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoiling suggests indulging, but here it means ruining.
explanation.definitionFit: Damaging something harms or ruins it, which is what spoiling it does.

clue.text: Boards trains, the way to travel at one time!

definitions.text: the way to travel at one time

parts.note: the boards is the theatre stage
to train someone is to coach them

explanation.surface: Someone climbs aboard trains, once the way everybody travelled.
explanation.walkthrough: Boards and trains look like a passenger getting on, but they are the stage and verbs of tutoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse-drawn stagecoaches were the standard public transport between towns before the railways.

clue.text: A lid's raised and closed — it's often chipped

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: a lid is a top, joined to A
a door pushed to is closed

explanation.surface: A lid is lifted and shut on a pot, which is often chipped.
explanation.walkthrough: Chipped sounds like damaged crockery, but it means cut into chips.
explanation.definitionFit: Potatoes are very often cut into chips, the British word for fries.

clue.text: Rise obtained, dances round!

indicators.note: turned round, the letters move into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A promotion is won, and everyone dances about in celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend is to go up or climb, which is what rising means.

clue.text: Broken arm hid gap forming midriff

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces that can be reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An injured arm covered a hole in someone's middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The diaphragm is the muscle dividing chest from abdomen, and midriff is an old name for it.

clue.text: Greeting man on top of hoist

parts.note: he is a man
ave is Latin for hail

explanation.surface: A man waves hello from the top of a lifting crane.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, on top of means the man is written above the greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave is to lift or haul with great effort, as one hoists a load.

clue.text: Overcharges to see castles?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: swindles or cheats a customer
second meaning: the chess pieces also called castles

explanation.surface: Someone is charged too much to visit historic castles.
explanation.definitionFit: To rook someone is slang for cheating them, and in chess the rook is the castle piece.

clue.text: Overlooking American hostility to Capone, the brute

indicators.note: overlooking means ignoring or leaving out, so letters are dropped

parts.note: animus is ill will
US is short for American
Al Capone, the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: Setting aside American hatred of the gangster Capone, he was a brute.
explanation.walkthrough: ANIMUS without US leaves ANIM, followed by Capone's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal is a beast, and brute is a word for a beast as opposed to a human.

clue.text: I ordered lady to meet sweetheart by swamp

parts.note: taken as written
a nun is a woman in a religious order
a date is a romantic partner

explanation.surface: Someone arranges for a woman to meet her beloved beside a marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: Ordered looks like an anagram signal or a command, but an ordered lady belongs to a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: To inundate is to flood or overwhelm, and swamp is used the same way as a verb.

clue.text: Ring for autograph before famous film

parts.note: to autograph is to sign
ET is Spielberg's well-known film

explanation.surface: Phoning to get a star's autograph ahead of a well-known film's release.
explanation.walkthrough: Ring looks like a phone call, but it is a finger ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A signet is a finger ring bearing a seal, used to stamp wax on documents.

clue.text: Daisy has nothing which identifies a heavenly body!

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like flower
O looks like zero
ID is short for identification

explanation.surface: A woman named Daisy discovers she can recognise nothing in the night sky.
explanation.walkthrough: Daisy reads as a person's name but is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: An asteroid is a small rocky body orbiting the sun, a kind of celestial object.
